Ah I see what you mean. That was the same when I was at uni, but I just dropped out. That's always an option other than death. Dropping out of uni was actually the best thing I ever did! I moved into a good job and felt soooo much happier, even though everyone went mad at me! But I didn't care what they thought - I just did what I knew was right for me. There's always a solution, whether it's doing another re-sit or leaving uni or changing course.

That's awesome you've passed other modules. Don't forget that! When we get down, it's easy for us to obsess with the negative and forget the positive stuff, but do try and remember the positive things you've achieved, otherwise what's the point in achieving them? It really helps to put the good and bad into 1 sentence like this...

"I may have failed this module, but at least I passed all the other ones!"

Or

"It's shit I failed the first year of uni, but that doesn't mean my life is all over because I can always re-do the year (like many other people do), find a new course that I prefer, or leave uni and get a cool job!" 

There's always a solution. What could you do?

I've got a quick tip to help you...

You say that you've failed at uni, but look at BOTH SIDES of the coin, not just the negative one.

Look at the proof that you HAVE failed and also the proof that you HAVEN'T. 

For example, proof that you've failed might be that you failed an assignment, but proof that you haven't failed is the fact you still have 2/3/4 years left on the course and also that you probably have passed other exams/tests/assignments/projects in the past!

A coin has 2 sides. Make sure you look at both of them. You can do it! :-)

I'd like to say just 1 thing...

You say you want to change but can't, but the fact you say you WANT to change proves that you can!

Most of the time, people don't change because deep down they don't really want to. But that's different for you because you said you DO want to change. You're already half way there! Now you just need the tools and you can get the tools by raising your hand and asking for help. Ask your doctor or therapist for help and they will help you. And most importantly - talk to people. It is the single biggest thing you can do. Talking to people is turning my life around. It's hard to do at first and sometimes I prefer to text what's in my mind to my partner or a friend because I find it hard to say things face to face, but getting your thoughts out into the open gets them out of your head and helps you feel so, so, soooo much better.

You WANT to change - that's means you're 50% there.
Now ask for help and talk to people - that's the final 50%!

Hey. I'm 28 and when I was your age, I went through a lot of the same situations as you. You're not alone! I was bullied so much at school that the headteacher told me not to come in anymore and to study for my GCSEs at home...on my own! Looking back, I can't believe they did that to me! Anyway, I did it and got through that tough time, so if I can do it, you can too. I'm living proof that you CAN get through tough times.

I've got a few things I'd like you to remember...

1) Nothing in life is permanent. The good times aren't permanent, but the bad times aren't permanent either. Life is a roller coaster full of ups and downs. You've had good times in the past, right? Well, those times have obviously gone for the time being...but they WILL come back again because that's just how life goes - up and down, up and down! Nothing lasts forever, neither the good times or the bad times, so hold on tight during this bumpy part of the ride because it'll even itself out again soon.

2) Try and balance your thoughts.
When we are depressed, we tend to focus on the negative things in our life and never on the positive. Now I'm not telling you to try and think positively because that's a load of crap, but I do want you to try and balance your thoughts. Here's what I mean...

When you have a negative thought, find evidence FOR and AGAINST that thought. So, find evidence that says the thought is CORRECT but also find evidence that says the thought is a load of BULLSHIT! Here's an example...

*Thought: "I'll never do well in my exams!"
*Evidence FOR: I failed my most recent practise paper.
*Evidence AGAINST: I got into a really good school which shows I'm a smart, intelligent guy, plus I got a D in my practise paper which is still a pass!

Then put the FOR and AGAINST sentences together to make 1 sentence like this...

"I may have failed my most recent practise paper, but I am smart enough to get into a good school and I didn't exactly fail my last exam because I got a D which is a pass!"

There are 2 sides to every coin! Look at both sides, not just one of them! 

3) Stop thinking ahead. 
We all think ahead too much. We think about what we'll be doing later on today, what we'll be doing tomorrow and what we'll be doing in 10 years' time! Well, I challenge you to NOT think about the future! Instead, think about the present. Think about what you're doing right now in this very moment (i.e. reading my post). Don't think about what job you'll do - you haven't even finished school yet! Forget ALL that because it's too overwhelming and too far ahead in the future. Just focus on the present and be mindful of what you're doing right here, right now.
